The annex endpoint-limit step (lines 288-296) writes only the lower end (inf F is the limit at minus infinity) and disposes of the upper end with 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument' (line 296), a 'similarly'-type elision. That unwritten upper-end fact (F(n) increases to F(inf)=sup F, including the case sup F = infinity) is used at lines 383-385 and 387-391 for truncations of targets with b = infinity, so the countable covering bound for unbounded targets (395-399), the second partition condition, the premeasure, existence of mu_F with mu_F(I(a,inf))=F(inf)-F(a), and mu_F(R)=F(inf)-F(-inf) (401-407) rest on a step that is not written. Covered once the upper-end case is written (finite supremum: a point x0 with F(x0) > sup F - eps and monotonicity for all x > x0; infinite supremum: a point with value above any prescribed bound and monotonicity).

defect_observations.observation: Upper-end endpoint-limit case is 'the reversed argument' (line 296); basis of the C008 partial verdict. The written lower-end sentence 'choose a point below any prescribed finite bound' should say a point whose F value is below the bound.

'The hypotheses on F make it a Stieltjes measure function with F(-inf)=0 and F(inf)=1' is asserted without the one-line codomain/tail-limit inference, and the probability-measure conclusion relies on C008, whose unbounded-target step is the one left unwritten. Not counted as a C012 gap because the C012 proof's own steps are written.

thm:p15-cdf-laws is stated for two real random variables. Here it is applied to the measure mu_F, and the bridge (mu_F is the law of the identity map, or a direct pi-lambda argument on rays) is left implicit. The cited proof's ray/pi-lambda argument does apply to any two Borel probability measures.

'Its values on bounded intervals are finite' is immediate for bounded half-open members (F(b)-F(a) with finite endpoints). For other bounded intervals, the step of containment in some (a',b'] plus monotonicity is not written.

'Durrett's generalized inverse construction': the construction is Durrett's (thm 1.2.2), but Durrett calls the map 'the inverse of F' and writes F^{-1} (printed p.11, PDF 19). The handbook's term and its notation Q_F do not record Durrett's name or notation.

The handbook's semialgebra definition requires the empty set and allows the empty union. Durrett's definition (printed p.3, PDF 11) lists only intersection closure and the complement property; the empty set appears only in his Example 1.1.5. The difference is not flagged, although the chapter says it follows Durrett's construction.
'need not be additive there' is asserted, but no non-additive outer measure is exhibited anywhere on the route. The remark is expository.
'it is not sigma-finite' is asserted without its one-line reason: only the empty set has finite premeasure, so no finite-premeasure cover of R exists.
No multidimensional Stieltjes construction (Durrett thm 1.1.11, rectangle-increment condition, printed p.7, PDF 15) was found on the P15 route. The boundary only excludes it.
